logline: The most powerful esper alive is a soft-spoken middle schooler who would rather be liked than feared - and the gap between what Mob can do and what he chooses to do is where all the interesting questions live.

renewal.note: Three-season run concluded December 2022 after 37 episodes plus OVAs; the manga adaptation is complete.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.5 series overall; Bones' Season 1 animation was described by critics as a visual language unto itself - abstract, expressive, deliberately anti-realistic in a way that mirrors Mob's relationship to power. Rotten Tomatoes entry tracks the franchise as a critical favourite.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 launches with the cleanest statement of thesis in ONE's catalogue: Mob Kageyama can demolish buildings with a thought, and none of that matters as much as whether the girl in his class notices him. Bones' animation is extraordinary in a way that is almost impossible to describe in text. It does not animate realistically, it animates emotionally, with color theory and frame distortion doing work that dialogue would undercut. The Body Improvement Club, which has no psychic powers and is included purely for motivational comedy, is one of the best recurring supporting groups in contemporary anime. The contrast between Reigen Arataka, Mob's fraudulent mentor, and Mob's genuine ability gives the series its central satirical engine. Season 1 establishes every character and thematic tension the next two seasons will develop. The only honest criticism is that the back half escalates slightly faster than the character work can absorb.

episode_reviews.title: Self-Proclaimed Psychic: Reigen Arataka ~And Mob~
episode_reviews.review_body: Mob Psycho 100 Season 1 Episode 1 aired July 12, 2016 on Tokyo MX as the premiere of Bones' adaptation. IMDb audience reviews describe the premiere as immediately establishing the show's visual and thematic identity. The episode introduces Mob and Reigen in twenty-three minutes that function as a tonal manifesto: Reigen is explicitly a con man, Mob is completely aware of this, and they have a functional working relationship anyway. The animation style announces itself in Mob's first full-power release - brief, visually staggering, and immediately contextualised as something Mob finds distressing rather than satisfying. The gap between what Mob can do and what he chooses to do is the show's central subject, stated in full in the first episode. IMDb audiences scored the series 8.5 overall.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere introduces both Mob and Reigen in a single twenty-three-minute loop that is also a complete tonal manifesto. Reigen is a con man; Mob is completely aware of this; they have a functional working relationship anyway. The animation style announces itself immediately - this show draws power differently from how any other anime draws power.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Mob's first full-power release - brief, visually staggering, and immediately contextualised as something he finds distressing rather than satisfying.

critic_note.text: A debut that immediately establishes Mob Psycho 100 as something entirely its own.

bollymeter.basis: CBR and multiple critical outlets mark Season 2 as the franchise's creative peak - the Keiji Mogami arc and the seventh division battle are cited as delivering animation and emotional payoffs that exceed Season 1. Audience scores on IMDb run above 9.0 per episode in the back half.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 is where Mob Psycho 100 decides it is a character drama that happens to have the best action sequences in contemporary anime, rather than the other way around. The Keiji Mogami possession arc is the series' darkest extended sequence - a villain whose worldview the show has the confidence to make partially convincing before dismantling it - and the extended fight through the seventh division headquarters involves Bones deploying techniques that critics compared to theatrical animation. The show's central thesis deepens in Season 2: Mob's restraint is not weakness, it is wisdom the adults around him do not have. Reigen's arc across this season - his relationship to fraud, to Mob, to his own sense of worth - is the best character writing the show produces. The penultimate episode is cited by multiple critics as a career-defining animation showcase. No filler. Thirteen episodes of escalating craft.
seasons.season_over_season: A genuine upgrade across every dimension - writing, animation ambition, emotional depth. Season 2 is the reason the franchise is spoken of alongside the medium's best.

episode_reviews.title: Cornered ~True Identity~
episode_reviews.review_body: Mob Psycho 100 Season 2 Episode 5 'Cornered ~True Identity~' aired February 4, 2019 on Tokyo MX as the episode multiple critics and IMDb audience reviewers identify as the franchise's character-writing peak. The season earned an 8.8 on IMDb. IMDb user reviews described it as 'Mob Psycho 100 at its character-writing peak - a complete short story inside a season-long arc.' The Reigen spotlight takes the series' central satirical figure - a con man who uses fraud to help people - and delivers his confrontation with his own dishonesty through a speech rather than a battle. The episode works entirely through character pressure rather than action spectacle, which is the correct judgment for a series where the most powerful being in the room often refuses to fight.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Reigen spotlight episode brings together everything the season has been building about his relationship with his own fraud and his genuine care for Mob. It works entirely through character pressure rather than action spectacle.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Reigen's speech - a con man talking his way out of a situation using only the truth.

critic_note.text: Mob Psycho 100 at its character-writing peak - a complete short story inside a season-long arc.

bollymeter.basis: The concluding season lands the character arcs the first two seasons established with unusual precision. Critical consensus marks it as one of the most satisfying anime finales in recent memory - resolving Mob's development without overwriting the ambiguity that made him interesting.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 earns the franchise a reputation for closure that few multi-season anime achieve. Where most serialized animation either extends past its natural end or stops mid-story, Mob Psycho 100 finds a finale that resolves every major emotional thread with proportionate weight. The Telepathy Club's arc, which occupied background space across three seasons, receives a payoff that comes across as a clear signal of the writing's confidence. The final action sequence involves Mob confronting something internal rather than external, a choice that could have felt anticlimactic and instead reads as earned restraint. Bones' animation in the final run matches Season 2's best. A three-season run that peaked in the middle and landed its ending cleanly, rarer in anime than it should be.
seasons.season_over_season: A satisfying and unusually graceful series conclusion - the show knew when to stop.
